root_cause.text: In `drivers/power/supply/max77705_charger.c`, the driver created a private workqueue with `create_singlethread_workqueue()` but did not bind its lifetime correctly to the devm-managed IRQ resources, so probe/remove paths could destroy or leak the workqueue while threaded IRQ handlers could still schedule work on it, causing a use-after-free window and missing cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `create_singlethread_workqueue(dev_name(dev))` with `devm_alloc_ordered_workqueue(dev, "%s", 0, dev_name(dev))` and removes the manual `destroy_workqueue(chg->wqueue)` error path; the commit message explicitly says the driver “leaks the memory on remove()” and that “probe error paths will not use a reversed order” because IRQs are freed by devm after the workqueue, allowing the interrupt handler to schedule work on freed memory.

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert charger probe setup to use a device-managed ordered workqueue and streamline error handling by removing manual workqueue cleanup.
intent_record.what: In max77705_charger_probe(), the code replaces create_singlethread_workqueue(dev_name(dev)) with devm_alloc_ordered_workqueue(dev, "%s", 0, dev_name(dev)); removes the explicit destroy_workqueue(chg->wqueue) cleanup path and the destroy_wq label; and changes several error paths to return immediately, using dev_err_probe() for initialization/enabling failures and direct return ret for IRQ request failures.
intent_record.how: The workqueue is now device-managed, so it will be automatically torn down with the device instead of requiring manual destruction on probe failure. This simplifies probe error handling, avoids leaking the workqueue on early returns, and keeps the existing failure reporting for charger initialization and enablement while preserving immediate propagation of IRQ request errors.

grouping_result.intent: Convert charger probe setup to use a device-managed ordered workqueue and streamline error handling by removing manual workqueue cleanup.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by replacing the manually managed private workqueue with a device-managed ordered workqueue, which fixes the lifetime mismatch with IRQ resources and removes risky manual cleanup.

candidates.rationale: This creates a privately owned workqueue whose lifetime is manually managed, which is the root of the bug: it is not bound to the devm-managed IRQ resources, so IRQ handlers can still queue work after the workqueue has been destroyed or leaked.
Manual destruction of the workqueue on probe failure highlights the lifetime mismatch; if any threaded IRQ or deferred work can still reference it, this teardown creates a use-after-free window.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement creates a privately owned workqueue with manual lifetime management. Because it is not devm-bound to the IRQ resources, threaded IRQ handlers or deferred work can still attempt to queue work after the workqueue has been destroyed or before cleanup completes, creating the use-after-free/missing-cleanup window described in the root cause.

This manual teardown is part of the lifetime mismatch: the workqueue can be destroyed while IRQ handlers or other deferred paths may still reference it. That can leave a window where work is queued to freed memory, matching the vulnerability root cause.
